title: The Fox Kit and the Little Miracle

pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a little red fox kit with a white-tipped tail, white socks on every paw, and curious amber eyes. The fox kit lives in a cozy den beneath the roots of an old oak tree.

The den beneath the roots is warm and soft, smelling of dry leaves and pine. Every evening Mama Fox sings a quiet little song, and {name} falls asleep snuggled right against her side. Every night here feels like one long, cozy lullaby.
One morning, the den feels strangely quiet and strangely special. In the soft nest sleeps a tiny new baby — warm and small as a mitten. {name} peeks closer and blinks those amber eyes in wonder.

Now Mama is with the baby every single minute. She rocks the little one, keeps the little one warm, and sings the old evening song — only very softly now, and not for the fox kit. {name} listens from the side, and their fluffy tail droops all by itself.

{name} finds the shiniest pebble in the whole forest and carries it home to show Mama. "Hush now, hush," Mama whispers. "The baby has only just fallen asleep." And suddenly the pebble doesn't look so shiny after all.

"Everyone has forgotten about me," thinks {name}, and their nose prickles like dandelion fluff. Nobody notices the shiny pebble, or the droopy tail. So the fox kit decides: it is time to find a place where little foxes always get noticed.

Early in the morning, {name} slips quietly out of the den — only the white tip of a tail flickers between the ferns. The forest breathes with dew and cool morning air. Somewhere out there must be a place where a fox kit truly gets noticed!

First comes the secret path between the tall ferns — the one that only {name} knows. The leaves tickle their nose, and the path winds along like a green tunnel. Even the air here smells like adventure.

Right in the middle of the green tunnel, {name} suddenly stops. The baby doesn't know this path at all — not one little bit! The thought flutters inside the fox kit's chest, warm and tickly and brand new.

Next comes a sunny clearing where the sweetest wild strawberries in the forest grow. {name} picks one little berry — and it tastes like summer itself. "Oh, if only the baby could see where the reddest ones grow," whispers a small voice deep inside.

Beyond the clearing waits the best puddle in the whole world — round and warm, with little clouds floating inside it. {name} takes a running leap: Splash! The drops fly all the way up to their ears, but somehow laughing all alone sounds a little quieter.

By the puddle hops a young hare named Flop, with his tiny little sisters all around him. He shows them how to jump the farthest of all, and they gaze up at him like a true hero. {name} watches from the side — and something stirs warmly inside.

"Being the big one is the best job in the forest," says Flop, proudly straightening his long ears. "I find the paths first, and I get to show my sisters every single wonder first!" {name} listens very, very carefully.

On a warm tree stump, {name} sits very still and thinks about the baby. That tiny black nose, paws like flower petals, the sleepy little snuffle: puff, puff. And the fox kit's heart turns as soft as the moss underfoot.

And then all the thoughts click together like a puzzle! The fox kit has a whole treasure box: a secret path, the sweetest strawberries, and the finest puddle in the world. {name} knows so many forest wonders — and every one of them is waiting for the baby.

"Home!" — and {name} dashes back through the ferns, the white tail-tip waving like a little flag. The forest rustles along, cheerful and glad. This time the fox kit is not running away from the den — but straight toward it, as fast as paws can go!
At the sunny clearing, {name} stops for just one minute. The ripest, reddest strawberry is laid upon a wide green leaf — a present for the baby. The very first present from the older fox kit.

By evening the forest turns golden, and the familiar smell of home comes tickling that little nose. There is the old oak, there are the dear old roots beneath it. A happy heart drums along: tap-tap, ta-dum!

By the den's doorway stands Mama Fox, watching the path. The moment she spots the red fur, she rushes forward first. "I was so worried, my little sunshine!" — and her nose nuzzles softly against one small ear.

"I never, ever forget about you," Mama says quietly. "My love is like the stars above the forest — enough for you, enough for the baby, and still some left over." {name} buries their nose deep in Mama's soft warm fur.
In the nest, the baby opens two round eyes, shiny as dewdrops. {name} gently reaches out a paw, and tiny little paws wrap around it, oh so tight. Oh, how warm this little one is!
"I will show you the secret path," {name} whispers to the baby. "And the strawberries, and the best puddle in the whole wide world. Just grow a little first."

Mama Fox opens her arms wide, wide, and gathers both little ones in at once. {name} sits inside the warm hug right beside the baby, and the den grows as bright as a summer clearing. There really is enough love for everyone.

Outside, the forest falls softly asleep, and inside the den the baby snuffles gently. {name} drifts off close by — no longer the littlest fox, but the big one now, with a whole treasure box of wonders for tomorrow. Good night, sweet little fox!
